prior_null.note: the ungated layer is already null with power; this module tests only whether compartment gating changes that

limits: HPA subcellular location is immunofluorescence across the Atlas's own cell lines, not a measurement in K562 or in the DepMap panel. Two proteins sharing an HPA annotation may not share a compartment in the cells these endpoints were measured in
iPTMnet aggregates enzyme-substrate relations across experiments, tissues and assay types with no cell-type field, so the edge set itself is not a K562 edge set and gating cannot make it one
the transcript endpoint is the wrong physics for a phosphorylation layer, stated before the run rather than after. It is included for comparability with the published null

co-dependency is a correlation across a cell-line panel. A kinase and its substrate correlating in dependency is consistent with a functional relationship and is not evidence of the phosphorylation event

genes annotated to many compartments are well-studied genes. The matched controls bin locations-per-pair exactly and the shuffle preserves per-gene compartment count, but neither removes publication depth itself, which this project has repeatedly found to be among the strongest nuisance covariates

the shared and disjoint arms are not independent samples of one population -- which genes have disjoint annotations is itself informative (organelle-restricted proteins are a specific kind of protein), so the head-to-head compares two biologically different sets of pairs
only 5 compartment shuffles are drawn, against 20 matched draws inside each arm. The shuffle sd is therefore the least precisely estimated quantity in the verdict
verdict: NEITHER THE ENDPOINT NOR THE COMPARTMENT GATE RESCUES THIS LAYER, AND THE ENDPOINT COMES CLOSEST. On CO-DEPENDENCY across 1,150 DepMap lines -- a readout that does not pass through transcription -- all 4,205 kinase/enzyme->substrate pairs sit at 1.139x their own decile-matched control (100% of 20 draws below observed). That is a layer with something in it, and it is the same layer ptm_sites measured at 0.992x on transcript response with a minimum detectable ratio of 1.075. The edges were not the problem; the endpoint was. SPECIFICITY, AND IT IS WHERE THE RESCUE GOES: 516 of 4,302 pairs (12%) are ALSO a PPI edge or co-complex, and PPI already predicts co-dependency in this project at 1.208x on the fast test. Removing them leaves 3,709 pairs at 1.037x, so 73% of the excess over 1.0 is carried by that 12% of pairs. What remains is still consistently above its own control (100% of 20 draws below observed) but sits under this project's own 1.05x bar for an interesting ratio, so the honest reading is that the enzyme->substrate relation adds little once physical association is accounted for: this is largely the PPI and complex layers wearing a phosphorylation label, which is the same category of error as `sl` wearing a synthetic lethality label. GATING: shared-compartment pairs reach 1.180x and disjoint pairs 1.063x, a gap of +0.116x. Permuting compartment IDENTITY across genes while preserving how many compartments each gene has gives +0.022x (sd 0.052, 20 draws), so the gap is not separated from what annotation depth alone produces -- promiscuously annotated genes share compartments with everything and are also better studied. The gate is NOT DETECTED as useful, which is not the same as shown useless. Endpoint B (transcript response) came back at ratio 2.26 with an sd of 0.93 across draws, so its interval spans 1.0 comfortably: it is UNINFORMATIVE, not a large effect and not a null. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: a compartment annotation is an immunofluorescence consensus over the Atlas's cell lines, not a measurement in K562 or in the DepMap panel, so 'shares a compartment' means shares an annotation. And co-dependency across a cell-line panel is consistent with a functional relationship without being evidence of the phosphorylation event itself.
